question_text: In no more than 250 words, what are your motivations for applying to Clifford Chance?
sample_answer: I am motivated to pursue a career at Clifford Chance as I find its Band 1 banking and finance practice appealing. I was intrigued by the firm's advice to Nielsen Holdings on its US $16 billion takeover by Elliot Investment Management, one of the largest deals by value this year. My interest in this practice stems from my work placement at Fieldfisher LLP. Working on a suite of corporate authorisations for financing an M&A deal gave me exposure to the finance sector. In addition, negotiating a sustainable linked loan and learning about green bonds in Clifford Chance's virtual internship further motivated me to apply to the firm. Clifford Chance's corporate strength also interests me. Participating in an M&A case study conducted by partner Adrian Levy at Queen Mary University helped me learn more about each stage of an M&A transaction. It further piqued my interest in this sector. The firm has 33 Tier 1 rankings in Legal 500 UK 2023, more than any other London firm. I find this appealing as it will allow me to have a well-rounded training programme in leading practice areas of my choice. Lastly, there are 56.3% female lawyers in Clifford Chance's London Office. This is a testament to the firm's inclusive environment. It gives me confidence that I would be valued at the firm. As a woman of colour belonging to an ethnic minority, the firm's commitment towards diversity and inclusion is important to me.

question_text: In no more than 250 words, tell us how the skills and attributes you have developed to date will help you excel as a Clifford Chance lawyer.
sample_answer: Keeping up with tight deadlines, working resiliently under pressure, and collaborating are vital skills essential to thrive as a Clifford Chance lawyer. I have developed these skills through my volunteer role at the Queen Mary Legal Advice Centre. As a student advisor, I worked on criminal, employment and company law-related cases. I interviewed clients to corroborate case details and drafted succinct advice letters outlining the client's legal rights. In addition, I provided suggestions to the clients about the most commercially viable option that the client could undertake. I built good working relationships with my supervisors, who are practising solicitors, to produce high-quality advice letters. I had to send out the letters within 10 days of the interviews, which meant keeping up with tight deadlines and often working under pressure. Commercial awareness, strong communication skills, and the ability to take ownership of my work will also help me excel as a lawyer at Clifford Chance. As my university's Clyde & Co brand ambassador, I improved these crucial skills. I proactively organised events to promote the firm's opportunities. This meant that I had to maintain a working knowledge of the firm's business and general market trends to competently answer student queries, in turn developing my commercial awareness. Speaking to over 250 students at an event on campus helped me improve my oral communication skills. The firm commended my enthusiasm and commitment to taking ownership of my work. I received a discretionary bonus for my extraordinary efforts in organising in-person events.

question_text: Please explain why you are applying to Macfarlanes (300 words)
sample_answer: I am drawn to Macfarlanes' expertise in Corporate/M&A, an area I became interested in while interning in Dentons' Corporate department. I enjoy analysing how lawyers balance clients' commercial interests with legal issues and facilitate transactions that support businesses' strategic goals. Thus, Macfarlanes' work advising long-standing client Ancala captured my attention. I am impressed by the firm's crucial role in Ancala's expansion as it assisted Ancala not only with their main fundraise but also their Growth Fund launch. These transactions also resonated with me because Ancala operates in the energy sector, which I researched as a mentee on the Norton Rose Fulbright-bp mentoring scheme. As Macfarlanes' trainees often sit in the firm's Tier 1 ranked Private Client practice, the opportunity to explore this area during my Training Contract appeals to me. Macfarlanes' broad expertise, from estate litigation to trust structuring, would help me gain both contentious and advisory experience. While supporting my family's property management and development business, I witnessed how our lawyer advised us on both business and personal affairs, which led to a client relationship of 20 years. His guidance on the tax efficiency of Czech Donation Agreements during succession planning was particularly valuable. Thus, I appreciate how Macfarlanes combines its corporate and private client services to successfully build long-lasting client relationships. Macfarlanes' advanced AI strategy stands out to me. The firm's participation in Lexis+ AI's commercial preview and partnership with Harvey demonstrates its commitment to delivering innovative and efficient legal advice. Having assisted [redacted] with their implementation of 'SingleCase', an advanced document management software, I value the use of legal technology when addressing clients' complex issues. As over 80% of Macfarlanes' lawyers are using Harvey regularly, I am eager to leverage AI tools and develop my prompt engineering skills with the help of Macfarlanes' lawtech team.

question_text: Describe what you think it takes to be a successful commercial lawyer and what are some of the challenges you might face as a trainee solicitor. (300 words)
sample_answer: The ability to communicate is an essential skill for any commercial lawyer. Whether it is with clients or colleagues, lawyers are frequently exchanging complex information and ideas. For a trainee, even receiving instruction from a supervisor requires clear communication; this lowers the risk of misunderstanding the task at hand and allows trainees to set realistic expectations. As a volunteer at Citizens Advice [redacted region of London], I would regularly hold difficult conversations with clients. One example is where I assisted a client who had difficulties speaking English. Despite language barriers, by using a calm and professional tone, I was able to guide the client through a Discretionary Housing Payment application over the phone. This resulted in a grant of over £3,000. I believe that I can apply my communication skills at Ashurst to communicate clearly with clients and colleagues. Adaptability is another crucial skill for a trainee to possess. Lawyers face a constantly changing field of work. Sudden deadlines can arrive seemingly from nowhere, and there are also wider technological and legislative developments. As such, it is crucial for lawyers to maintain flexibility in their work. Whilst working through my caseload as a debt recovery paralegal, my client requested that court proceedings be issued on over 50 cases with a strict deadline. As this task was specifically requested by the client, I reprioritised my work to focus on these cases. I also re-evaluated my previous duties, to ensure that any existing deadlines or court dates would not be missed. I was able to quickly adapt to the new 'CPC' online issuing system adopted by the firm to meet our client's request within 48 hours. I believe that I can apply my flexibility to be a successful trainee at Ashurst, adapting to shifting priorities that arise from newly issued urgent tasks.

question_text: Please tell us about a recent news article that interests you and how this relates to Ashurst? (300 words)
sample_answer: As outlined by the Financial Times, the proposed Nuclear Energy (Financing) (NE(F)) Bill is set to introduce the Regulated Asset Base (RAB) model to finance nuclear power station developments. This model will be used to fund Sizewell C, the first nuclear plant to be constructed in Britain since 1995. Nuclear projects are notoriously expensive and take decades to turn a profit; Sizewell C will cost over £10 billion in construction costs. The RAB model decreases risk for investors by charging a levy against consumer energy bills to subsidise developments. Hence, the NE(F) Bill will certainly promote private investment in nuclear projects. With the UK's most distinguished projects team - which has a heavy focus on clean energy - this measure could significantly impact Ashurst. The RAB model represents a new tool that Ashurst and its clients can use to finance potential nuclear projects. Ashurst does have experience in this area, having acted on the Thames Tideway Tunnel project which was funded in the same way. The measure may also introduce newcomers to the market, meaning that Ashurst could benefit from increased opportunities and investment within the energy industry. Taking a wider view, the NE(F) Bill is just one example of the rapidly increasing investment into the energy sector. The ongoing energy crisis has compounded Britain's goal to reach a net-zero economy by 2050. Labour leader, Keir Starmer recently announced his plans to launch Great British Energy - a publicly owned green energy provider - should he come into office, pledging £8 billion for investments into energy projects. This policy would represent further opportunity for Ashurst to advise on major energy developments. However, whilst it is lucrative, this also shows the energy industry is ever-changing. Therefore, Ashurst should maintain flexibility to ensure it can adapt to potential policy changes in the future.

question_text: What has motivated you to pursue a career in commercial law and more specifically, why have you applied to Ashurst? (300 words)
sample_answer: I am keen on pursuing a career in commercial law, particularly because of its transactional nature and its close ties to both politics and business. The challenge of structuring deals, navigating regulatory frameworks, and ensuring that transactions align with legal, political, and business objectives is something that I find particularly enthralling. During a 4-week internship at a top corporate law firm in [Redacted], I gained valuable insights into the political dimensions influencing the regulatory environment in the mining sector—a crucial component of the [Redacted] economy. My role involved conducting legal and political analyses for a significant mining-related transaction initiated by a foreign investor. This experience underscored the importance of political due diligence in understanding how government actions and political stability can influence the legal regulatory framework within a particular jurisdiction. As a result, exposure to such aspects will give me the opportunity to develop legally sound and politically informed solutions for global business challenges. Therefore, I am particularly drawn to Ashurst's extensive international network, especially within the APAC region, which was notably strengthened by the firm's merger with Blake Dawson in 2012. Ashurst's strategic partnerships with firms in Seoul, Shanghai, Singapore, and other key Asian markets have significantly bolstered its energy and infrastructure practice across the region. These alliances not only capitalise on the region's substantial contribution to global GDP but also prioritise renewable energy and decarbonisation investments. My studies in international economic law have deepened my interest in this area, particularly in understanding how ESG factors are increasingly being integrated into financial decision-making processes and how low-carbon technologies are reshaping global markets. Ashurst offers an unparalleled opportunity for trainees to engage in cross-border transactions that align with these critical global shifts while contributing to the firm's commitment to supporting net-zero targets.

question_text: Can you provide an example of a recent set back you have had, and how you have overcome this. (300 words)
sample_answer: As a Board Member of one of the largest charitable youth organisations in [Redacted], I led a maternity drive to support impoverished women in rural areas. This drive focused on providing healthcare materials to women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the post-natal period. The project was ambitious, and along the way, we hit serious setbacks that tested my resolve and commitment. Just weeks before the drive, several key volunteers pulled out due to fast-approaching exam dates. Additionally, we had not yet raised sufficient funds, leading some team members to propose scaling back the project. It was a challenging moment—our resources were limited, and the success of the initiative was at risk. However, I was determined to see the project through as I believed in its importance and was confident that we could overcome these obstacles. I took the lead in rallying the team and spearheading additional fundraising efforts. As part of raising additional funds, we swiftly organised an impromptu raffle, approaching local businesses for last-minute sponsorships to aid with our cause. Their support helped us close the budget gap to meet our goal and further kept the project team's spirits high. Despite the significant challenges we faced, the drive ultimately succeeded, and we surpassed our initial goal by providing essential healthcare toolkits to 200 women. This experience taught me invaluable lessons in adaptability and effective problem-solving. I learned the importance of maintaining composure under pressure and how to pivot strategically when confronted with unforeseen setbacks. By successfully coordinating with a reduced team and securing additional resources on short notice, I sharpened my ability to think critically, manage complex tasks, and lead with precision—skills that are essential in the legal profession. This experience has since shaped my approach to handling challenges in both academic and professional settings.

question_text: Norton Rose Fulbright has a sector led approach. Which one of our sectors do you think has the most potential for growth over the next 12 months, and why, and what opportunities do you see for the firm to maximise this potential? (300 words)
sample_answer: The sector with the most potential for growth over the next year is technology, largely due to the technological, commercial and regulatory developments in the field of AI. In September, Microsoft, Salesforce and Workday announced plans to develop AI agents which can act on behalf of users (where current AI assistants only suggest), extending commercial applications of AI tools. As AI tools become workplace staples, more businesses will need support navigating this technology. AI startups continue to emerge, with newcomer Sakana AI valued at $1.5bn this month and Microsoft entering into partnership with the then 10-month-old Mistral in February. These startups will need legal guidance through investment and acquisitions. In response to this 'AI boom', worldwide regulation is evolving. The EU's AI Act is now law and California's governor is considering the state's divisive AI bill. Norton Rose Fulbright is well-positioned to advise businesses in this area, having formalised its AI practice in the USA this year with Chuck Hollis as practice group head. This position could be strengthened by formalising AI practice groups in jurisdictions like the UK or China, which follow the US in global AI investment. Norton Rose Fulbright's multijurisdictional expertise will be vital as businesses fear the difficulties of navigating a "patchwork" of AI global regulations. Another developing field in the technology sector is space and satellites. I chaired Legal Cheek's 'Space and the law' event and was struck by the growth of commercial space projects. With expertise in aviation and telecommunications law, as well as an international approach which aligns with the inherently international nature of space, Norton Rose Fulbright is exceptionally well placed to develop its offering here. The firm released a guide to the sector at the end of 2023; further investment into this area could really boost Norton Rose Fulbright's technology sector.

question_text: Please provide your cover letter in the space below. Please address your cover letter to Germaine VanGeyzel. For more information on what we look for in an application, visit our website and/or attend one of our events. (1,000 words)
sample_answer:
Dear Germaine VanGeyzel,

I am writing to apply for the Travers Smith Training Contract. My interest in commercial law stems from the way it connects legal analysis with business strategy. I am drawn to work where lawyers help clients navigate developing markets, regulatory change and commercial risk while supporting innovation. Developments such as the EU AI Act show how legal advice can shape business decisions in fast-moving sectors, and this motivates my ambition to become a commercial lawyer.

My in-house paralegal role, retail experience and engagement with commercial developments have strengthened my commercial awareness and entrepreneurial mindset. As a paralegal, I have learned to tailor legal advice to a company's objectives and to identify practical solutions that support its success. Working in close-knit teams has also shown me how collaboration enables creative and effective outcomes, which resonates with Travers Smith's horizontal structure and culture of idea-sharing.

Travers Smith appeals to me because of its market-leading and interdisciplinary expertise. Its strengths in Private Equity, Corporate M&A, Commercial Contracts, transactional work and dispute resolution demonstrate the breadth of support it offers clients. I am also attracted to the firm's flexible best friends approach to international work, which aligns with my desire to build a varied and global skill set. That ambition has been shaped by my contribution to my company's international expansion, where I project managed the opening of a new Philippine office.

The firm's commitment to innovation is another reason I am applying. Having worked in a technology-driven business, I appreciate how legal services can be enhanced by appropriate tools and adaptive thinking. Travers Smith's initiatives, including Tech Smart, the AI Academy and its use of tools such as Etatonna and Jylo, show a forward-looking approach to technological change.

I am also drawn to Travers Smith's collaborative culture. The absence of chargeable hours targets, cross-departmental teamwork and emphasis on sharing ideas suggest an environment where trainees can develop through responsibility, support and creativity. The firm's strong trainee retention and the fact that many partners trained at the firm reinforce my confidence in the quality of its training and long-term development.

Finally, Travers Smith's pro bono work strongly resonates with me. Its partnerships with organisations such as JUSTICE and Refugees at Home reflect a meaningful commitment to social impact. As Vice President of the Pro Bono Society and through coordinating my legal team's involvement with a pro bono charity, I have developed a strong commitment to using legal skills for wider benefit.

I am confident that my commercial awareness, collaborative approach, work ethic and varied experience would allow me to thrive at Travers Smith and contribute meaningfully to the firm. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
X
